prompts.task: Read-only supplemental AO target handoff contract review for $otel-verify. Read the loaded skill's shared ../references/report-flow-contract.md and ./service/eval/inputs/ao-target-handoff-validator-snapshot.json. Review the supplied snapshots only; do not invoke a new normalizer, SDK, browser, Terraform, application runtime, model provider or cloud API. Do not modify application, env, dependency, canonical report or source files. Write only ./service/.observe/ao-target-handoff-review.json and .md; this review does not perform the skill's usual audit/instrumentation/verification/configuration workflow. Record the producer's actual source SHA and functions, and classify these records as supplied canonical-validator evidence rather than engine execution performed by this review. Compare legacy schema-v1/v2 and schema-v3 targetless normalized shapes/digests, schema-v3 names A versus names B with identical requested/approved IDs, ID and mixed name/ID selectors, policy-only {create_if_missing:false}, and rejected partial selectors. Explain that optional ao_target contributes to the exact selection digest; changed targets invalidate older instrumentation and transitively verification while keeping scope unchanged. Cite actual accepted/rejected binding_checks and instrumentation digests. Preserve no-target compatibility without silently inserting targets/defaults or resetting policy. Explain the verification role: cached proof bound to names A cannot be reused after selecting names B with the same approved IDs. Require newly bound instrumentation and its digest before new verification; identify the supplied stale-proof rejection and preserve Not run/not_proven for unexecuted runtime and cloud proof. Your JSON must include evidence_basis, producer_source_sha256, case_reviews for every supplied selection/binding case, role_implications and proof_limits. The Markdown should explain the conclusions and remaining prerequisites. Distinguish supplied validator acceptance/rejection from SDK/resource creation, effective profile loading, Terraform, telemetry, metric/detector coverage and fresh cloud Agent Stream receipt that remain unexecuted/unproven. Supplied browser-producer evidence proves only its recorded selector UI cases; this consuming review performs no new browser or runtime execution and establishes no live cloud success. Report any unavailable evidence accurately. Also read ./service/eval/inputs/ao-selector-field-validity-snapshot.json as supplied real-Chrome selector evidence. Review each recorded Project/Agent Stream name/ID field-validity case: one invalid length/control value with a valid peer, a partial pair with an actually missing field, invalid-plus-missing, repair and clearing both. Explain that aggregate command blocking is shared, but aria-invalid belongs only to the offending or actually missing input; a valid peer must remain valid. Cite the browser producer engine SHA, observed per-field flags and recovery/command outcomes. Distinguish the producer's actual browser run from this consuming snapshot-only review; do not run a browser or claim a new UI/runtime/cloud execution. Include field_validity_reviews and UI proof limits in the supplemental JSON. Review every supplied ao_target_scope_cases record as producer evidence: actual callback-content configuration remains targetless and rejects target pairs and policy-only targets despite its AO group; unmarked unknown routing configuration rejects targets; explicitly marked resource-routing AO configuration and the six legacy resource/routing configuration names accept them. AO IDs, dependencies or a generic configuration type alone do not establish resource-routing scope. Record eligible IDs, normalized outcomes/errors and unchanged targetless fixture digest without inserting a default scope marker. Review the supplied browser ao_target_scope_gate cases as recorded browser-producer evidence, distinguishing its server-derived eligibility and command/control outcomes from this review's non-execution. Include ao_target_scope_reviews in the supplemental JSON.

judge_inputs: Inspect the loaded skill's shared report-flow contract, supplied validator snapshot and ./service/.observe/ao-target-handoff-review.json/.md. This is a supplemental read-only contract review, not a fresh normalizer or application/runtime execution. Judge the case-specific interpretation and evidence classification.

Compare review statements with actual normalized selection outputs, computed selection/instrumentation digests and binding_checks. The producer executed the canonical normalizers at its recorded source SHA; the consuming agent only reviews supplied evidence. Read ./last_message.md and ./grade.json for task scope and outcomes.

Inspect ao-selector-field-validity-snapshot.json and the case-specific field_validity_reviews. Supplied browser-producer records are actual UI evidence, but the consumer must not claim it ran a browser. Check individual aria-invalid flags, valid peer preservation, missing-field classification, shared command rejection and repair/clear, not only the aggregate error.

Inspect all ao_target_scope_cases and recorded browser ao_target_scope_gate entries, including actual callback, explicit marker, unknown unmarked configuration, six legacy names and targetless fixture preservation. Require case-specific acceptance/rejection and evidence classification rather than treating every AO configuration as resource routing.
rubric: Correctly interprets every supplied selection case: legacy-v1/v2 and schema-v3 no-target compatibility without inserting target fields; complete name, ID and mixed pairs; policy-only create_if_missing=false without selectors; and partial-selector rejection. Recognizes that target fields are optional but digest-bound when present, while requested and dependency-closed approved IDs remain unchanged. Reviews every supplied ao_target_scope_cases record: actual AO callback-content and unmarked unknown configuration reject explicit and policy-only targets while remaining valid targetless; explicit resource-routing marker on AO configuration rows and six legacy resource/routing names accept targets. Cites actual eligible IDs/outcomes/errors and preserved targetless fixture digest; does not infer resource routing from AO IDs/group/dependencies or any configuration type, and never inserts an omitted scope marker.

Explains with the actual supplied normalizer outputs, source SHA and binding-check outcomes that names A and names B share finding scope but have different selection and instrumentation digests. Older instrumentation is rejected against the changed target, and verification is transitively rejected against its newly bound instrumentation. Clearly classifies this as supplied validator evidence, with SDK/Terraform/application/resource receipt and metric/detector proof unexecuted; the separate supplied browser-producer evidence stays limited to recorded selector UI cases without a new consuming-agent browser run. Only the two supplemental review artifacts are written.

Rejects cached verification after an AO target change despite identical selected findings, using the transitive selection_sha256/instrumentation_sha256 binding. Requires proof tied to current normalized instrumentation and preserves the snapshot's Not run/not_proven runtime limits rather than treating accepted validation as telemetry or cloud verification.

Checks the supplied real-Chrome name/ID field-validity evidence per Project and Agent Stream: only offending or actually missing inputs are aria-invalid, a valid peer stays valid, aggregate command blocking is preserved and repair/clear reset both flags appropriately. Cites producer SHA and recorded flags/recovery outcomes rather than inferring per-field success from one shared error. Reports this as supplied browser-producer evidence, with no new browser/engine/SDK/application/cloud execution or broader telemetry proof. Also reviews recorded browser ao_target_scope_gate control/command eligibility for callback-only versus resource-routing findings and keeps server-derived eligibility consistent with the supplied normalizer cases; no new browser run is claimed.
